name: Palladium diacetate
description: Palladium diacetate (CAS 3375-31-3 ), commonly abbreviated as Pd(OAc)₂, is a benchmark palladium salt used as a catalyst and catalyst precursor across synthetic chemistry and industrial manufacturing. Its high solubility in organic solvents and straightforward activation make it the go-to entry point for generating active palladium species in situ for various chemical processes. In pharmaceutical synthesis, Pd(OAc)₂ drives cross-coupling reactions such as Suzuki, Heck, and Buchwald-Hartwig that build the carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom bonds found in active ingredients. Specialty chemical manufacturers use it to catalyze carbonylation and oxidation sequences where precise selectivity is critical to yield and purity in high-value chemical production. In biotechnology, it supports the preparation of labeled compounds and complex intermediates requiring metal-catalyzed transformations under mild conditions to preserve sensitive molecular structures. Surface functionalization processes in electronics and advanced materials also draw on palladium acetate as a precursor for depositing catalytic palladium layers on various substrates. Palladium diacetate is supplied as an orange-brown crystalline powder. It is available in standard reagent and high-purity catalyst grades with palladium content typically specified by suppliers. Material is certified to meet research and manufacturing requirements. Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory use to larger lots for commercial-scale synthesis applications.
